lanes.why: T-0154 amends three closed-programme oracles, which operator ruling Q-015 (2026-09-12) says may change only by a dated amendment authored by a session other than the implementer, for the one rule or key the ruled item fixes. The same lane writes the batch's own acceptance oracle, because the two must agree about what each gate now sees. Committed before dispatch.

The five gate fixes and the two baselines that hold what they now see. Disjoint from the oracle lane: the implementer touches no test file the oracle lane claims. read-only-actually-reads.test.ts was added mid-batch: its header states in the present tense that the shared helper mocks api-auth wholesale, which tests-13 makes false. The independent review found it outside both lanes, which is a gap in this file rather than in the work.

note: Two lanes, which is the cap at org/policy.json:125. An integrator writes and commits this file before any dispatch; lanes receive claims and never acquire or mutate them. T-0153's record says its implementer amended its own frozen oracle and the reviewer caught it; here the closed-oracle amendments are the ORACLE lane's from the start, which is what that ruling asks for. The REVIEWER that high-assurance requires reads the diff and writes nothing, so it holds no lane.
